regime_context: A clear semiconductor/AI complex leadership exists: Memory-HBM (rank 1, score 2.42, crowded, trend) leads AI Infrastructure (2.0) and Semiconductor Equipment (1.41), but the one-narrative flag is false, breadth of rotation is narrowing (eligible 20/49 = 0.41), and absorption is low (0.31). theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is the strongest eligible theme that is NOT crowded-out of the AI/semi complex. Rank 4, score 1.31, eligible=true, hurst_tag=trend, durability_bar=0.68 (highest among top-5 eligible), and breadth=0.5 (much better cohesion than the rank-1 Memory theme's breadth=0.0). It shares the 'trend' characteristic but has real breadth, suggesting a durable trend rather than a one-name squeeze. Crowding_z=1.93 is high, so this is a stay-with-trend, keep-size-modest lean, not an add-on-strength lean.
theses.dissent: Cybersecurity is crowded (z=1.93, crowded=true) — among the most crowded names in the ranks; if the AI complex sees a drawdown, crowded software/protection names could see correlated exit with no basket-level edge to time it.

falsifier.text: CIBR breaks below its own 21-day simple moving average while SPY holds above its own

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The rank-1 headline theme has breadth=0.0 and val_state='diverging', meaning the leadership score is carried by a tiny subset of names and price is diverging from some internal measure. Hurst_tag=trend and eligible=true argue against actively fading, but breadth 0.0 plus crowded=true plus low absorption (0.31) means this is a concentration, not a theme-wide durable rally. Under the guardrails I cannot fade it on a crowding flag, but I also cannot justify overweight on a rank that is explicitly not a return forecast. The honest lean is avoid/no new concentration.
theses.dissent: Hurst_tag=trend and eligible=true mean the absolute-trend discipline says stay unless the trend itself breaks; avoiding a confirmed trend leader can mean missing the strongest move while it lasts.

falsifier.text: Breadth rises above 0.5 for a full week (leadership broadens beyond the current narrow carrier)

theses.subject: Energy (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Energy is the strongest non-tech, non-AI trend candidate: US Energy Complex (rank 7, eligible=true, hurst=trend, durability_bar=0.54, breadth=0.045) and Energy EW (rank 19, eligible=true, hurst=trend). Crowding is low (z=0.56 and -0.13). This is a humble diversification lean — a trend-gated, vol-aware theme outside the crowded semiconductor complex, which is exactly what the validated drawdown-control edge rewards (non-correlated lower-vol participation). Low conviction because breadth is thin and this is grounded in the trend gate, not any alpha signal.
evidence: gate_helps=true (drawdown discipline is the validated edge)
theses.dissent: Energy rank 7 is middle-of-pack and its score (0.775) is far below the leadership scores; a low-score trend name has little momentum support and the modest-or-none relative-momentum verdict says rank positioning has no edge.

falsifier.text: XLE closes below its own 21-day simple moving average for three consecutive sessions
